## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pūtimukhapetavatthu* (Pv 3) is a text within the *Petavatthu* collection concerning the karmic consequences of verbal misconduct. In the narrative, a hungry ghost explains the danger of harsh speech, lying, and slander [Shirker]. The ghost—a former monk who is encountered floating in mid-air by the elder Nārada—exhibits a striking contrast: while possessing a radiant, heavenly body, he is tormented by a worm-infested, foul-smelling mouth as retribution for his past slander [Shirker]. The peta implores Nārada that compassionate and skilled teachers should caution others never to engage in slander or falsehoods [Shirker]. The story's background involves two austere monks residing harmoniously in a village setting, touching upon the status of a *puthujjana* (an uninstructed worldling lacking the insight of noble disciples) [Shirker].
